questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had to learn italian, so for this reason it made a lot of sense to go to Italy

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I felt like my university was lacking some information upon arrival.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I want to the university office to get help, and they always helped solving my problems.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found it through a housing app. It was okay, but also difficult to deal with an italian landlord

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: They should try to find a person who speaks the native language in order for them to help with talking to the landlord.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They did not even have me registered, even tough they through email several times had confirmed my arrival and confirmed my application.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Normally people have to show up, and their name would be shown on a list, but mine wasn't there, and this menat that I had to register (again) at the university office.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The university office where very helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: 100% succesful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Maybe contact them before hand to make sure that they have registered your name.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I was doing language courses, so I was more or less only doing things related to this.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different. I was like going to school again, but I think that is pretty regular when you have to learn a whole new language.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Corso della lingua Italiana
CLID corso della lingua Italiana B1
Corso della cultura Italiana
"Performance" di fonetica

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Well, for me it had to be these specific courses, I did not get any other options. But this was also because I only was there to learn Italian.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
We had to pay an agent for us to find our apartment, and that did cost us 50 euro. 
Going to the doctor did also cost 20 euro.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The cost is more or less the same as in Denmark. It is cheeper to go out though and coffee dosen't cost as much.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was no offers for anything else.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: We went to other cities when we didn't have school, in order to see some other parts of italy.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: To go see other places when they are in Italy, because it's cheaper then traveling there form the home country.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very difficult. Normally Italians are quite open, but Siena is something different. Because of the Palio, they are very closed and don't really let other people in. But we found other Italians who where not from Siena, which was very nice!

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go out and try to talk to people at bars, maybe.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: To communicate about bureaucracy in italian was difficult.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food, the language and the people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Try to contact the university by phone before going there. 
Go to class as recommended, because you will miss out on a lot even if you only skip one class. 
Know that some of the subjects you will be taking are very similar to some of the stuff you already have been learning.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You will have to take a lot of the same courses just in order to gain points, which in my opinion seems quite useless, but if you don't do it, you won't gain all of your ECTS points.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Learning italian so well as I did, and also to have met so many lovely people from different cultures.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To learn the language. Italian has so many different times of all kinds, which can be very challenging.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
